paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates negative log probabilities associated with clinically relevant tokens, comparing a baseline model (MistralV0.2-Base) with the same model fine-tuned on data from six different medical specialties. The x-axis displays the six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, listed from left to right. The y-axis represents negative log probability, with a linear scale ranging from approximately -27 to -22, and is labeled "Negative log probability." For each specialty, two bars are presented: one representing the baseline model in a light blue color, and one representing the fine-tuned model in a shade of orange. The baseline model consistently appears on the left side of each pair and generally shows higher (less negative) values compared to the fine-tuned bars. The Gastro-fine-tuned bar consistently appears as the shortest of the orange bars, with a value close to -22, while the Infect-fine-tuned bar consistently appears as the tallest, reaching slightly below -23.  The bars are not sorted in any obvious order, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond the color differentiation.
